html:
Global diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the conflict in Ukraine saw a US envoy meet with Vladimir Putin, resulting in the release of an American citizen, even as Kyiv was hit by Russian missiles. Simultaneously, tensions surged in the Middle East, leading the US to order its diplomats to evacuate Saudi Arabia amid ongoing Houthi attacks and an Iranian shift to an "offensive" defense doctrine.

Russia-Ukraine: Russian missiles struck Kyiv, injuring six people, just hours after Moscow signaled readiness "in principle" to resume US-mediated peace talks. US President Donald Trump stated the world was "the closest we've been" to ending the war. Donald Trump’s envoy, Steve Witkoff, met with Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg, where Putin ordered the release of American Stephen Hubbard, who had been jailed for over four years. Reports indicate Russia is pushing for a summit including Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war, without Ukraine or the EU. Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed support for a ceasefire and trilateral talks with the US and Russia.

Middle East Security: The US has ordered all embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia following an attack on King Fahd airport that killed one and injured eight, alongside sustained Houthi attacks on the kingdom. The Saudi-led coalition claimed to have intercepted multiple drones. The UK is deploying fighter jets to help protect Saudi Arabia from these attacks, and Egypt’s Sisi stated Egypt would defend Saudi territory but rules out an attack on Yemen. Iran’s IRGC has adopted an "offensive" defense doctrine, threatening invasion, and claimed mines halted tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. While indirect talks on a ceasefire proposal with Iran continue, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi affirmed Iran will "never surrender" to US power. Netanyahu declared that "toppling Iran’s regime" was a "primary objective" after discussing Iran with US War Secretary Pete Hegseth, adding that Khamenei released the safety catch and Iran is trying to develop "death bombs." Reports suggest the US and Israel are planning an attack on Iran after the midterm congressional elections, though Donald Trump reportedly refused a prior attack and some Israeli officials oppose immediate action.

Global Economy & Tech: Tech giants face scrutiny, with Meta fined $25 billion for "lies" over user data privacy, the largest such fine to date. Meanwhile, Elon Musk is reportedly plotting a "mega-merger" of SpaceX and Tesla, which he says has "a lot to be gained." Oil prices rose amidst escalating tensions in the Middle East and reports of decreased US crude oil and gasoline inventories.

Climate & Environment: Indonesia is grappling with its worst wildfire season in a decade, fueled by peat fires. A UN climate report found that the Paris Climate Agreement’s 1.5-degree Celsius warming target is no longer achievable, noting a major increase in US climate pollution. Super Typhoon Champi, one of 2026’s strongest storms, churned across the Pacific towards Taiwan and eastern China, having already slammed Guam. Some Britons are relocating north to escape increasingly hot summers, a trend that may emerge in the US.

Domestic Crises & Unrest: India faces a political crisis after 130 million names were struck off voter rolls in what is described as the largest disenfranchisement in history. Sudan’s war continues to escalate, with drone strikes across Sudan killing more than 160 people in recent days, including 153 in Abyei. In Australia, lawmaker Helen Haines lost both legs after a car attack, and a man was arrested for allegedly threatening staff at Hannah Beazley’s electorate office while armed. France also banned protests in parts of Paris after violent unrest, with an NGO suggesting pro-Russian accounts amplified anger online.

US Political Landscape: US midterms remain a contentious focal point, with US President Donald Trump praising a supporter for allegedly punching a protester at a South Carolina rally. France’s President Emmanuel Macron appeared to accuse US President Donald Trump of exploiting French unrest for political gain ahead of these elections. The influential pro-Israel lobbying group AIPAC announced it would halt direct contributions and endorsements to candidates, though its affiliated super PAC will continue. The Justice Department’s "likely" noncitizen voter list in California was deemed "unreliable" by officials.
